title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth projective variety of dimension d. A^i (or A_{d-i}) is the group of cycles of codimension i (dimension d-i) modulo numerical equivalence, tensored with R. In the notation of this page and the surrounding notes:
- P_i^+ is the (closed) cone spanned by effective cycles of codimension i, i.e. the pseudoeffective cone.
- P_i^{+0} is the dual cone: classes that meet every effective cycle of complementary dimension non-negatively. In modern terms these are the 'nef' classes.

The page is a working sheet on positivity of intersection numbers.

(1) Opening question. If a divisor D satisfies D.C >= 0 for every effective curve C (D is nef), does D^i.X_i >= 0 hold for every effective i-dimensional cycle X_i? Formally: D in P_1^{+0} implies D^i in P_i^{+0}?

(2) Induction strategy. Assume as induction hypothesis ('hyp. de réc.') that D^i is in P_i^{+0} for i <= d-1. It remains to show D^d is in P_d^{+0}, i.e. the number D^d is >= 0. Write D^d = D^i . D^{d-i} with 0 < i < d, the two factors lying in P_i^{+0} and P_{d-i}^{+0}.

(3) Reduction to a cone statement. It would suffice that P_i^{+0} . P_{d-i}^{+0} >= 0. Grothendieck notes, correctly by cone biduality, that this is equivalent to either of:
- alpha_i(P_i^{+0}) is contained in P_{d-i}^+;
- alpha_{d-i}(P_{d-i}^{+0}) is contained in P_i^+.
Here alpha_i identifies codimension-i classes with dimension-(d-i) classes. In words: 'nef classes are pseudoeffective'. Both follow from the stronger multiplicativity P_i^{+0}.P_j^{+0} contained in P_{i+j}^{+0} ('the product of nef classes is nef').

(4) Unconditional argument for divisors, d = 3. Assume:
- D.C >= 0 for every effective curve C;
- D^2.D' >= 0 for every effective surface D'.
We want D^3 >= 0. Take D' ample (P_1^{+0} sits in A^1, which maps to A_2, which contains P_2^+). Then D' + nD has positive intersection with every curve and every surface. By Nakai–Moishezon it is ample, so it lies in P_2^+ and (D'+nD)^3 > 0. Expanding,
(D'+nD)^3 = D'^3 + 3n D'^2 D + 3n^2 D' D^2 + n^3 D^3 > 0.
Dividing by n^3 and letting n go to infinity gives the boxed conclusion D^3 >= 0. The crossed-out 'D + (1/n)D'' is the same perturbation, rescaled.

This is exactly Kleiman's proof (1966) that nef divisors meet every subvariety non-negatively, i.e. the nef cone is the closure of the ample cone.

The page thus does two things:
- it reproduces the divisor case;
- it isolates the general higher-codimension question 'is a product of nef classes nef / are nef classes pseudoeffective?', which Grothendieck leaves open with '??'.
errors: No outright error. The step 'D'+nD ample' needs the Nakai–Moishezon criterion together with the induction hypothesis on surfaces; the page leaves this implicit.

The general cone question P_i^{+0}.P_{d-i}^{+0} >= 0 is left open with '??'. It is now known to be false in general: Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin (2011, abelian fourfolds) gave nef classes of codimension 2 that are not pseudoeffective, and products of nef classes that are not nef; Ottem gave further examples on hyperkähler fourfolds. So the stronger conjectural inclusion P_i^{+0}P_j^{+0} contained in P_{i+j}^{+0} cannot be used, beyond the divisor case where the page's perturbation argument works.

ideas.what: Nef divisors have non-negative top self-intersection and non-negative degree on every subvariety, proved by induction plus the perturbation D'+nD (D' ample), expanded binomially with n going to infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Kleiman's theorem: nef implies D^k.V >= 0; nef cone is the closure of the ample cone
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Kleiman, 'Toward a numerical theory of ampleness', Annals 1966
ideas.where_published: Kleiman 1966; Grothendieck's influence on Kleiman (IHES 1965) is known

ideas.what: Cones of effective cycles P_i^+ and their duals P_i^{+0} in numerical cycle groups, with the question whether duality alpha_i maps the dual (nef) cone into the effective cone.
ideas.modern_name: Nef cone contained in the pseudoeffective cone for higher-codimension cycles
ideas.where_published: Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968) discusses positivity cones in Grothendieck's program

ideas.what: Equivalence of 'nef_i . nef_{d-i} >= 0' with the two inclusions 'nef contained in pseudoeffective', and the stronger multiplicativity 'nef . nef contained in nef'.
ideas.modern_name: Cone biduality / positivity of products of nef classes

missed.claim: Around 1965 Grothendieck explicitly formulated, as an open question in his standard-conjecture notes, whether nef cycle classes are pseudoeffective, equivalently whether products of nef classes are nef. He reduced the positivity of powers of nef divisors to this question. The question was later answered negatively (DELV 2011), apparently without the literature attributing its early formulation to Grothendieck.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents that the nef-versus-pseudoeffective problem for higher-codimension cycles goes back to Grothendieck's positivity program accompanying the standard conjectures. It also shows that the divisor case (Kleiman's theorem) was worked out in his notes in parallel with Kleiman.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically, the page reproduces Kleiman's well-known argument. Its historical interest is the explicit early formulation of the higher-codimension question 'are nef classes pseudoeffective / is nef.nef nef', resolved negatively only in 2011; I am unsure whether this is credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'D^1.C' should read 'D.C' (D a divisor class); the superscript is a stray mark.
Third line: 'D^1 ∈ P_1^{+0}' should read 'D ∈ P_1^{+0}'.
The word read as 'aussi[?]' is uncertain, possibly 'annonce...' / 'à montrer'; the line asks whether D^d ∈ P_d^{+0}.
'A_2 ⊃ P_2^+': the arrow shows the map A^1 → A_2 (divisors as dimension-2 cycles on a threefold).
Bottom: the crossed-out expression is 'D + (1/n)D'', the rescaled perturbation.
